stories.title: Far-Right AfD Wins Landslide Victory in Germany's Saxony-Anhalt State Election
stories.summary: Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won Sunday's state election in Saxony-Anhalt with roughly 44.5% of the vote, more than double the 18.5% won by Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU), according to early results. The Left party took about 9.5%, the Greens 9%, and the Social Democrats 8%. The result makes the AfD the first far-right party to win a German state election since World War II, though it is expected to fall short of a majority, and rival parties have so far ruled out forming a coalition with it, leaving the question of who governs Saxony-Anhalt unresolved.

stories.title: Netanyahu Orders Removal of Unauthorized West Bank Settler Outposts Amid US Pressure
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered the dismantling of unauthorized West Bank settler outposts, according to sources, following pressure from the United States over settler violence against Palestinians. Israeli media reported the order targets roughly 100 outposts built without official state authorization across the occupied territory. The move follows U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee's weekend condemnation of violent settlers as "terrorists" who should face severe consequences, made after he met Palestinian Americans in a West Bank town. It was not immediately clear when the removal operation would begin.

stories.title: Investors Brace for Pivotal Week as ECB Rate Decision and US Inflation Data Loom
stories.summary: Markets enter the week focused on Thursday's European Central Bank rate decision, with traders fully pricing a 25-basis-point hike to 2.50% after eurozone inflation accelerated to 3.3% year-on-year in August, the highest since September 2023, driven by a 14.3% jump in energy costs. In the US, the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the September 16 meeting eased to about 50% from 68% earlier in the week after Fed Governor Christopher Waller struck a dovish tone, with Friday's August CPI report now the key test. Oil has still climbed roughly 10% over the past week to $91.74 a barrel amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict, while gold rose 0.5% to $4,476 an ounce and Australia's central bank faces rising pressure for a fourth rate hike this year after stronger-than-expected GDP growth.

stories.title: 'Model Fatigue' Sets In as AI Labs Race to Release New Models at Breakneck Pace
stories.summary: Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google all shipped major new AI models within the same week in early September, prompting what CNBC described as "model fatigue" spreading across the industry. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said labs are "all moving to faster cadences," partly because teams returned from summer vacation, while Runpod CEO Zhen Lu said IT managers, CFOs and founders are spending outsized hours comparing model costs and capabilities only to see the comparisons go stale before they finish. The rapid release cadence, combined with limited regulatory clarity, has also stoked concerns about deploying increasingly capable models without adequate safeguards in place.

stories.title: Princeton's New AI Framework Controls Fusion Plasma Faster Than Any Human Operator
stories.summary: Researchers at Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory and Princeton University have developed an AI framework called PACMAN that can monitor and control fusion plasma in about 20 milliseconds, far faster than a human operator's reaction time of several seconds. Tested in five experiments on the Department of Energy's DIII-D National Fusion Facility tokamak, the system predicted a dangerous "tearing mode" instability roughly 200 milliseconds before it appeared and adjusted the plasma to prevent it, and separately coordinated all six of the reactor's microwave heating systems at once to hit research targets. The framework, described in a new paper in the journal Nuclear Fusion, keeps hardware safety limits and human-set objectives in place while letting multiple machine-learning models work together, and its developers say its modular design could make it adaptable to future fusion reactors.

stories.title: Bad Bunny's Super Bowl Halftime Show Wins Record 7 Emmys at Creative Arts Ceremony
stories.summary: "The Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show Starring Bad Bunny" won seven awards at Saturday's Creative Arts Emmys in Los Angeles, more than any Super Bowl halftime show in television history, including the top prize for Outstanding Variety Special (Live). The win marks Bad Bunny's first Primetime Emmy and makes the broadcast only the second Super Bowl halftime show ever to win the top program award, after the 2022 Pepsi Super Bowl LVI show. The special also picked up six technical honors, including best technical direction and camerawork, music direction, choreography, lighting design and sound mixing. The main Primetime Emmy Awards ceremony will be held September 14 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles.
